gloss: to be found; to be noticed

definitions.gloss: to be found; to be noticed; to be seen
definitions.explanation: To come into view or to be found when looking. Often used in the negative (見当たらない) to mean something cannot be found.

examples.japanese: {鍵|かぎ}が{見当|みあ}たらない。
{適切|てきせつ}な{候補者|こうほしゃ}が{見当|みあ}たらない。
examples.english: No suitable candidate can be found.

examples.japanese: {探|さが}していた{本|ほん}が{本棚|ほんだな}の{奥|おく}から{見当|みあ}たった。
examples.english: The book I was looking for was found in the back of the bookshelf.

notes:
USAGE:
Very commonly used in the negative form {見当|みあ}たらない (cannot be found). The affirmative form is less frequent but does occur. This is an intransitive verb — the thing being found is the subject.

ORTHOGRAPHY:
Also written as {見|み}あたる in kana, or {見当たる|みあたる} as a single unit. Despite the kanji {当|あ}たる, this is a distinct word from {当|あ}たる (to hit).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {見当|みあ}たらない (cannot be found)
- どこにも{見当|みあ}たらない (nowhere to be found)
- {特|とく}に{問題|もんだい}は{見当|みあ}たらない (no particular problems can be found)
